newsitem.title: DUBAI: GOLF-GREEN BEATS NORMAN AND WOOOSNAM IN PLAYOFF.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-GREEN BEATS NORMAN AND WOOOSNAM IN PLAYOFF.

text.p: Australian underdog Richard Green sank a 15-foot birdie putt on the first hole of a sudden death playoff against Greg Norman and Ian Woosnam to win the Dubai Desert Classic on Sunday.
The 26-year-old lefthander from Melbourne made his winning birdie after compatriot Norman and Woosnam missed their attempts.
Woosnam took a one-stroke lead into the last regulation hole but threw the title away when he chipped his approach into the water at the par five 18th.
The Welshman played safe by laying up short of the lake that guards the 18th green but he mishit his chip and it landed on the bank of the green and bounced back into the lake.
Woosnam then holed from 12 feet for a bogey six to get into the playoff after Green had made a 25-foot birdie and Norman a birdie from eight feet.
Norman shot a final round of 66, Green 68 and Woosnam 69 for 16-under-par aggregates of 272.
"To win this tournament against those guys is absolutely unbelievable. I'm just buzzing," Green, in his first full year on the European Tour, said.

Bernhard Langer held fourth place on his own after a closing 69, the German losing his chance when he shot a bogey six at the long 15th after leaving his second shot in the rough and then fluffing a chip.
Compatriot Thomas Goegele grabbed fifth place with a six-under 66 for a 13-under total of 275, but European number one Colin Montgomerie never mounted a challenge.
Two shots behind overnight, he came to grief at the huge lake that fronts the ninth and 18th greens and which he cleared so dramatically with his second shot at the last when he won last year.
This time he hit the water at the ninth on the way to a double bogey six and again at 18 for a bogey six as he compiled a 71. He shared sixth place on 276.
